trial_court: Court of Principal Judge, Family Court (Central), HMA No.206/10/08 (New No.61747/2016)
facts_of_case: The parties are Amitabh and Hemlata Bhasin. The wife sought enhancement of maintenance for their two minor children from ₹12,000 to ₹18,000 per month. The husband filed an application for review of the order allowing this, which was dismissed. He then applied for dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1)(a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, but his petition was adjourned sine die till payment of maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: Orders passed in pending proceedings prior to the transfer of jurisdiction are deemed to be orders of the Family Court.
legal_principles.held: Once the Statute has provided for pending proceedings to stand transferred to the Family Court constituted under the Family Courts Act and to be continued in the Family Court, the orders passed in the said proceedings of a date prior to the date of transfer and against which no remedies have been availed of till that date, are to be deemed to be orders of the Family court.

legal_principles.principle: The remedies against orders passed in transferred proceedings are governed by the law applicable after the transfer.
legal_principles.held: If the latter were to be the correct position, the appeal would lie under Section 19(1) & (6) of the Family Courts Act to be heard by a Division Bench of this Court.

outcome.final_order: The final court order dismissed the husband's appeal against the trial court's orders and adjourned the proceeding for dissolution of marriage sine die till payment of maintenance.
